data.section: Takeaway

title: ai_tools_workflows › Takeaway

body:
- **Bulk deals** (trades above 0.5% of listed shares) are reported by brokers to the exchange after market close. — [EquitiesIndia glossary](https://equitiesindia.com/glossary/bulk-deal-reporting); [EquityResearchIndia](https://www.equityresearchindia.com/post/block-deals-and-bulk-deals-how-to-track-big-institutional-trades-and-what-they-signal)
- **Block deals**: a SEBI circular dated 8 Oct 2025 raised the minimum block deal size from ₹10 cr to ₹25 cr and mandated delivery-based settlement, effective 7 Dec 2025. Sources conflict on whether details are disseminated in real time or after market hours. A block deal shows one trade, not the fund's total position. — [Kotak Securities](https://www.kotaksecurities.com/news/sebi-raises-minimum-block-deal-size-delivery-trade); [5paisa](https://www.5paisa.com/index.php/news/sebi-revamps-block-deal-norms-sets-rs25-crore-minimum-trade-size); [PolicyCircle](https://www.policycircle.org/policy/sebi-market-reform-bulk-deals/)
- **MF disclosures**: SEBI requires monthly portfolio disclosure on AMC websites. Debt close-ended/interval schemes must disclose by the 3rd working day (2009 circular), and average AUM must be filed with AMFI within 7 working days (2014). The current consolidated rules are in the SEBI Master Circular for Mutual Funds dated 20 March 2026. — [SEBI 2009 circular](https://www.sebi.gov.in/legal/circulars/mar-2009/circular-portfolio-format-for-debt-oriented-close-ended-and-interval-schemes-plans_14185.html); [Business Standard 2014](https://www.business-standard.com/article/markets/mfs-to-disclose-average-aum-on-monthly-basis-sebi-114040300039_1.html); [Taxmann on MCR revision](https://www.taxmann.com/post/blog/sebi-revises-monthly-cumulative-report-format-for-mutual-funds/)
- **Marcellus**: the "Consistent Compounders" framework rests on three pillars: competitive advantage (moat), capital allocation, and credible accounting. Its forensic model (based on Schilit's *Financial Shenanigans*) uses about 10–12 ratios to rank accounting quality. Companies are bucketed so that the cleanest sit in the top 3 deciles and suspected manipulators in the bottom 4. A second level of governance checks runs during deep-dives. Marcellus claims a strong link between accounting quality and shareholder returns (firm's own claim). — [Marcellus, Consistent Compounders PMS](https://marcellus.in/portfolio-management-services/marcellus-consistent-compounder-pms); [Marcellus MeritorQ newsletter](https://marcellus.in/newsletter/meritorq-pms/meritorq-forensic-accounting-using-quant-methods-boosts-returns); [Marcellus Jan 2020 PDF](https://marcellus.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Marcellus_Creating_Consistent-Compounders_Jan-2020-1.pdf); [Elearnmarkets, Diamonds in the Dust](https://www.elearnmarkets.com/school/units/diamonds-in-the-dust/marcellus-s-3-level-check-to-detect-accounting-frauds)
- **SPIVA India Year-End 2025**: the official summary says a firm majority of active funds in every category underperformed over the decade to Dec 2025. Large-cap figures differ between sources. Secondary reports give about 74% (3-yr), 84% (5-yr) and 76% (10-yr) underperforming, against the S&P India LargeMidCap benchmark, which some argue distorts the comparison. — [S&P SPIVA India YE2025](https://www.spglobal.com/spdji/en/spiva/article/spiva-india-year-end-2025/); [AngelOne](https://www.angelone.in/news/mutual-funds/most-indian-equity-funds-underperform-s-p-indices-over-10-years); [DSIJ](https://insights.dsij.in/dsijarticledetail/is-mutual-fund-alpha-still-alive-57107)

data.section: India

title: deep_dive_protocol › India

body:
| Item | Choice / approximation |
|---|---|
| PIT source | NSE `corporates-pit` date-range queries, 7-day chunks, broadcast 2020-12-01 → 2025-01-31 (218 files, 0 failures). 92,026 unique rows after de-duplication on (symbol, name, from, to, qty, mode, type). Spot check: for VSSL and GANECOS, every row returned by the per-symbol query was also in the range pull. Monthly row counts fall over time (≈3.4k/mo in 2021 → ≈1.6k/mo in 2024), with regular dips in trading-window months (Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct). I did not establish whether the fall is a reporting change or a real one (see caveat 5). |
| Qualifying buys | `acqMode = Market Purchase`, `tdpTransactionType = Buy`, `secType = Equity Shares`, category ∈ {Promoters, Promoter Group} → promoter; {Director, Key Managerial Personnel} → KMP. Dropped: "Immediate relative" (969 rows; the field does not say whose relative), "Other"/"-", and every other mode (Market Sale 40.7k, ESOP 18.7k, pledge rows 9.2k, off-market 2.4k, gift, inter-se, preferential, rights, scheme…). → **9,831 buys** (8,785 promoter, 1,046 KMP). Median trade → broadcast lag is 2 days (90th pct 5). |
| Event | Pre-registered 30-day rolling rule, ≥ ₹1 cr or ≥ 0.25% of equity. One per company per 365 days. Event = broadcast date. → **684 events** (619 promoter-only, 43 KMP-only, 22 mixed) in 2021–2024. |
| Shares outstanding | Not available point-in-time from a clean source. **Approximation:** implied total shares = `afterAcqSharesNo / afterAcqSharesPer × 100`, using PIT rows with holding ≥ 1% (rounding error ≤ 0.5%). Event mcap = implied shares × insider VWAP. Both come from the same disclosure, so they are unadjusted and consistent. |
| Control mcap | Implied shares (PIT row nearest in time, ≤ 365 d) × k × Yahoo close on the event date. k = unadjusted PIT market-trade price ÷ Yahoo close near the share row's date, which puts shares on Yahoo's adjusted basis. **Yahoo's split-event list is incomplete for Indian bonuses** (e.g. 360ONE 2023 shows 2:1, but prices are adjusted 4:1), so split events are not used. Universe = every NSE symbol with any PIT filing in the window (1,705 symbols; 80 have no Yahoo history). |
| Prices | Yahoo v8 `.NS`, adjusted close, ≥ 1.1 s per call. A long browser User-Agent got HTTP 429; `Mozilla/5.0` works. Benchmark ^CRSLDX (NIFTY 500 price index, so no dividends; used for context only). |
| Entry / horizons | First trading day strictly after the broadcast date; 63/126/252 trading days. |
| Controls | 5 random (seed 11) from the universe. mcap ×0.5–×2 of the event firm, listed ≥ 180 d, no own event within ±365 d, same entry day, no data-error jump (daily adj move outside −50%/+100%) in the 12m window. 351/351 events got 5 controls. |
| Stats | Mean, 1/99 winsorised mean, median, hit rate, naive t, 95% bootstrap CI resampling event-months (2,000). |

body:
1. **Concentrated filing dates.** Most 10-Ks are filed in February–March, so the 32 filing-month clusters are
   unequal and a few months dominate. The bootstrap CIs are wide and some per-year CIs are lopsided. Read the CIs,
   not the t-stats.
2. Three filing years and one regime (the 2021 speculative peak, the 2022 crash, the 2023 recovery). The paper
   covers 1995–2014.
3. Raw term-frequency cosine is dominated by stop-words (median 0.998). The paper's other measures (min-edit,
   simple) were not run. Jaccard (sets) behaved more like the paper.
4. Section extraction uses the longest heading-to-heading span. A cross-reference ("see Item 1A Risk Factors")
   can extend a span a little. Not hand-checked beyond spot tests.
5. Controls are size-matched only (no sector, momentum or value matching), and there is no factor regression.
6. One firm can appear up to 3 times (one per year). The month bootstrap does not cluster by firm.
7. Costs: 0.5% round trip applied to the avoid benefit only. Shorting is out of scope.

title: MY_MEMORY › 5. Stocks we've looked at (learning watchlist — NOT buy advice)

body:
**Business.** AAL makes M&HCV drive axles (rear/front, single and tandem, 7–70 t GVW), brakes and gear sets at Mysuru (main), Rudrapur
and Jamshedpur (Hosur closed Feb-2025 `[NSE 04-Feb-2025]`). FY26 revenue split `[AR26 n.21.1]`: axles ₹1,209 cr (56%), brakes ₹531 cr (24%),
others (gear sets, carriers, housings, suspensions, scrap) ₹437 cr (20%); exports ₹219 cr (10%, mostly to Meritor plants in Italy and the US).
**Ownership.** 35.52% BF Investment (Kalyani / Bharat Forge) + 35.52% Meritor HVS LLC (Cummins since 2022) = 71.04%; DIIs 15.4%; FIIs 0.8%;
23,260 shareholders (down from 34,527 in Dec-2023) `[SCR]`.
**Sales model change (the key structural fact).** Until FY25, ~80% of sales went to OEMs *through* Meritor HVS (India) Ltd (MHVSIL, a Cummins
group company): ₹1,668.6 cr of FY25's ₹2,077.5 cr `[AR26 n.35]`. Minority shareholders rejected the ₹2,500 cr FY26 material-RPT resolution with
MHVSIL on 14-Dec-2024 (20.53% for, 79.47% against) `[AR25 CG report]`. From 1-Apr-2025 AAL sells direct to OEMs and pays MHVSIL a **technical
fee** (₹97.5 cr in FY26) for marketing, engineering, account and programme management under a services agreement dated 31-Mar-2025, extended
on 29-Apr-2026 to **30-Apr-2027** ("no impact") `[NSE 29-Apr-2026]`. AAL is "in the process of finalising direct agreements with OEMs" `[AR26 n.1]`.
**Units (manufacturer + MNC-subsidiary rows):** (1) the **plant**: revenue capacity ~₹2,700 cr on the existing base `[T-Q4FY26]` vs a Q2 FY27
run-rate of ₹2,650 cr, so ~98% used; phase-1 capex ₹120 cr adds 20–30% `[T-Q2FY27]`. (2) the **product node**: axle per vehicle (single → tandem →
tractor-trailer raises content per vehicle). (3) the **channel**: Customer A = 66% of revenue (almost certainly Ashok Leyland). (4) the **parent
relationship**: fee, exports to group plants, warranty claims routed via MHVSIL.
**Peers:** GNA Axles (axles, mostly tractor/export), Jamna Auto (CV springs), Wheels India (CV wheels); P/Es 15.6 / 20.8 / 29.7 `[SCR 23-Nov-2026]`.

data.section: 2. Map (L1): what is the unit?

title: AUTOAXLES_live › 2. Map (L1): what is the unit?

body:
"Smallest operating unit" differs by model. Pick the unit(s) before L3.
| Business type | Units to rebuild | Typical micro-drivers to test first |
|---|---|---|
| Retailer / consumer service | Store (sq ft, bills, staff) | Rent, minimum wages, outsourced security/housekeeping, shrinkage |
| **Manufacturer** | **(1) Plant** (capacity × utilisation), **(2) product node/platform** (price, mix, competition), **(3) channel account** (OEM, dealer, distributor concentration) | Materials basket and pass-through lag, plant utilisation, regulatory product transitions, warranty |
| **MNC subsidiary / group company** | All of the above plus the **parent relationship** | Royalty, support/cost allocations, transfer-pricing formulas, purchases from and sales to group companies, dividends to the parent, renewal dates |
| **Lender (bank / NBFC; v1.3, see the adaptation section)** | **(1) Branch** (deposits, CASA, sourcing per outlet), **(2) loan segment/cohort** (yield, slippage, LGD), **(3) liability pool** (CASA, retail TD, NRI/FCNR, bulk), **(4) balance-sheet "cost lines"** (CRR, PSL shortfall, DICGC) | IBA wage settlement, deposit repricing lag vs EBLR share, DICGC premium, CRR/PSL rules, special funding windows, write-offs vs slippage, collateral price (gold LTV) |
| Platform / software | Cohort / account | CAC, retention, take rate |
| **US widely held company (v1.2)** | Same unit as its business type, plus **management as the "related party"** | KPI definitions (payback, comps, "adjusted"), SBC and retention awards, 8-K Item 5.02 pay and perks, Form 4 clusters, guidance-beat pattern |
